note: THE NAME, AND WHAT IT WRITES. Emacs answers ((u0-e1 error) "My error"): `define-error' is two `put's -- an `error-conditions' list whose CAR is the symbol itself and whose tail is the parent's conditions (nothing but `error' by default), and an `error-message' string. Nothing opaque is created, which is what makes the plist half of this item (u0-signal-consults-the-error-conditions-plist) the same feature and not a second one. 12 ELPA packages call `define-error', 66 times. kg answers `void-function' at this pin.
